taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Standard set, reasoning allowed. Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Spain (Madrid) is in the CET/CEST zone. In late September, daylight saving time (CEST, UTC+2) is still in effect (it ends the last Sunday of October).

ET in late September is EDT (UTC-4).

So Madrid (UTC+2) is **6 hours ahead** of EDT.

5:00 PM EDT = 17:00 EDT → 17:00 + 6h = 23:00 Madrid time, same date.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Peru (Lima) is in the **UTC-5** time zone and does not observe daylight saving time.

12:00 UTC − 5 hours = **07:00 local time**, same date.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST is Central European Summer Time, which is UTC+2.

Tokyo is JST, which is UTC+9.

The difference is 9 - 2 = 7 hours ahead of CEST.

So 9:00 AM CEST + 7 hours = 16:00 JST on the same date.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PDT is UTC-7.

Madrid in October is on CEST (Central European Summer Time), which is UTC+2. However, daylight saving time in Europe ends on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, that's October 25. So on October 11, Madrid is still on CEST = UTC+2.

Difference from PDT to Madrid local time: UTC-7 to UTC+2 = +9 hours.

October 11 at 11:59 PM PDT + 9 hours = October 12 at 8:59 AM Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PST is UTC-8. Madrid in March 2026 will be on CET (Central European Time), which is UTC+1 (before the clocks change — Spain's DST in 2026 starts on the last Sunday of March, which is March 29, so on March 3 Spain is still on CET = UTC+1).

The difference between PST and CET is 9 hours (CET is 9 hours ahead of PST).

March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST + 9 hours = March 4, 2026 at 08:59 AM CET.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1. Los Angeles in February is on PST, which is UTC-8. The difference is 9 hours (CET is 9 hours ahead of PST).

10:00 AM CET minus 9 hours = 1:00 AM PST.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

JST is UTC+9. Lima, Peru is UTC-5.

The difference is 9 - (-5) = 14 hours behind JST.

8:00 AM JST → subtract 14 hours → 6:00 PM (18:00) the previous day in Lima.

May 5, 2026 at 08:00 JST = May 4, 2026 at 18:00 Lima time.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PT (Pacific Time) in late October will be PDT (Pacific Daylight Time), which is UTC-7. However, I need to check: the US ends DST on the first Sunday of November, so on October 28, 2026, the US is still on PDT (UTC-7).

Madrid in late October: Spain ends DST on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25. So by October 28, Spain is on CET (UTC+1).

The difference: Madrid (UTC+1) minus PT (UTC-7) = 8 hours ahead.

11:59 PM PT on October 28 → add 8 hours → 7:59 AM on October 29 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

## Reasoning

ET (Eastern Time) on October 30, 2026 — I need to check if the US is on EDT or EST.

- The US ends Daylight Saving Time on the first Sunday of November. In 2026, that's November 1. So on October 30, the US is still on **EDT (UTC-4)**.

Madrid, Spain in late October — Spain ends DST on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25. So by October 30, Spain is on **CET (UTC+1)**.

Time difference: Madrid (UTC+1) vs EDT (UTC-4) = **+5 hours**.

9:00 AM ET = 9:00 AM EDT = 13:00 UTC+0 = **14:00 CET**

So October 30, 2026 at 14:00 Madrid local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1. New York in late October is on EDT (UTC-4), as Daylight Saving Time ends the first Sunday of November.

The difference is 5 hours behind CET.

18:00 CET → 13:00 EDT (New York time), same date.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PT (Pacific Time) in November is PST = UTC−8.

Madrid in November is on CET = UTC+1.

Difference: Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PT.

November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT → add 9 hours → November 3, 2026 at 08:59 AM Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PT (Pacific Time) in March 2026 — before the March 8 US DST change? Actually, US DST in 2026 springs forward on March 8, so by March 20, PT is PDT = UTC-7.

Madrid in March 2026 — Europe switches to summer time on March 29, so on March 20, Madrid is still on CET = UTC+1.

So the offset between Madrid and PDT (UTC-7) is UTC+1 minus UTC-7 = +8 hours.

March 20 at 11:59 PM PT = March 21 at 07:59 AM Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1. Los Angeles is in the Pacific Time zone.

On March 25, 2026, the US will have already switched to PDT (clocks spring forward on March 8, 2026), so Los Angeles will be on PDT = UTC−7.

Difference between CET and PDT: 1 − (−7) = 8 hours behind.

12:00 PM CET − 8 hours = 4:00 AM PDT on March 25, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

## Reasoning

**ET on October 12, 2026:**
- ET = Eastern Time (US)
- October 12, 2026 is in autumn in the US, so Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4) will still be in effect (EDT ends first Sunday of November).

**12:00 AM ET = midnight at the start of October 12 (i.e., 00:00 ET on October 12)**
- 00:00 EDT = UTC+4h = 04:00 UTC on October 12, 2026

**Madrid local time on October 12, 2026:**
- Spain observes CEST (Central European Summer Time, UTC+2) until the last Sunday of October.
- Last Sunday of October 2026: October 25, 2026.
- So on October 12, Madrid is still on CEST (UTC+2).

**04:00 UTC + 2h = 06:00 local Madrid time on October 12, 2026**

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) is UTC-12. Madrid is UTC+2 in summer (CEST). October 9, 2026 — Spain observes daylight saving time until the last Sunday of October, so on October 9 Madrid is still on CEST (UTC+2).

The difference between Madrid (UTC+2) and AoE (UTC-12) is 14 hours.

So 23:59 AoE on October 9 = 23:59 + 14h = 13:59 on October 10 in Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PT (Pacific Time) in August is PDT (Pacific Daylight Time), which is UTC−7.

Madrid in August is on CEST (Central European Summer Time), which is UTC+2.

The difference is 2 − (−7) = **9 hours ahead** of PT.

12:00 PM PT on August 14, 2026 → add 9 hours → 21:00 on August 14, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

## Reasoning

IST here refers to Indian Standard Time, which is UTC+5:30.

Madrid, Spain uses:
- CET (UTC+1) in winter
- CEST (UTC+2) in summer

November 10, 2026 falls in winter (after the last Sunday of October), so Madrid will be on CET = UTC+1.

**Converting:**
- Deadline: November 10, 2026 at 23:59 IST (UTC+5:30)
- Convert to UTC: 23:59 − 5:30 = 18:29 UTC on November 10, 2026
- Convert to Madrid (UTC+1): 18:29 + 1:00 = 19:29 on November 10, 2026

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

## Reasoning

**Nepal Time (NPT):** UTC+5:45
**Lima, Peru Time:** UTC-5 (Peru does not observe DST)

**Difference:** NPT is 10 hours and 45 minutes ahead of Lima time.

So I need to subtract 10 hours and 45 minutes from the Nepal deadline.

**Deadline in Nepal time:** April 2, 2026 at 17:00 NPT

Convert to UTC first:
- 17:00 NPT − 5:45 = 11:15 UTC on April 2, 2026

Convert UTC to Lima (UTC-5):
- 11:15 UTC − 5:00 = 06:15 on April 2, 2026

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

## Reasoning

**Adelaide time** = Australian Central Standard Time (ACST) or Australian Central Daylight Time (ACDT)?

October 6, 2026 — Australia is in the Southern Hemisphere. Daylight saving in South Australia starts in October. In 2026, DST in South Australia begins on the first Sunday of October.

First Sunday of October 2026: October 1 is a Thursday, so the first Sunday is **October 4, 2026**. DST starts then, clocks spring forward.

So on October 6, 2026, Adelaide is on **ACDT = UTC+10:30**.

**Madrid time** in October 2026: Spain observes CEST (Central European Summer Time) = UTC+2 until the last Sunday of October. The last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25. So on October 6, Madrid is on **CEST = UTC+2**.

**Conversion:**
- Adelaide: 10:00 AM ACDT = 10:00 - 10:30 = UTC 23:30 on October 5, 2026
- Madrid: UTC 23:30 + 2:00 = 01:30 on October 6, 2026

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

## Reasoning

I need to convert 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026 to Madrid time.

**Step 1: Determine Sydney's UTC offset on October 3, 2026.**

October 3, 2026 — Australia enters daylight saving time (AEDT) on the first Sunday of October. In 2026, October 4 is a Sunday, so DST starts on October 4. Therefore, on October 3, Sydney is still on AEST = UTC+10.

**Step 2: Determine Madrid's UTC offset on October 3, 2026.**

Spain (Madrid) observes CEST (Central European Summer Time) = UTC+2 in summer. DST in Europe ends on the last Sunday of October. So on October 3, 2026, Madrid is on UTC+2.

**Step 3: Convert.**

Sydney time: October 3, 2026 at 18:00 AEST (UTC+10)
UTC time: 18:00 - 10:00 = 08:00 UTC on October 3, 2026
Madrid time: 08:00 + 2:00 = 10:00 on October 3, 2026

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
